host.binding: numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 (all 48 CPUs of the single NUMA node), so 8 workers have 48 CPUs

command: dive-bench --set <shard-set.toml> --dive-bin ~/bins/dive --dive-revision 5bb880635f46c7266e015a0d812f18e4411cdc6a --profile default --workers 1,4,8 --reps 3 --timeout 3600 --xmx 24g on od-2..od-4; the moved repetitions ran the same command with --reps 1 on a set file holding the moved entries (scripts/perf/release/node/d4x.sh); each row records its repetition and node

raw.location: dive evidence archive bucket (us-east-1), prefix release-perf/2026-11-27-rc02/ (archive shardN is node od-N, small-node is node small)

deviations: Repetitions were moved between the five nodes of one type to finish sooner, without adding nodes: SlushLarge ran repetitions 1 and 2 on od-1 and 3 on od-4; od-3's repetition 3 ran on the small node; od-2's repetition 3 ran there up to MCNanoLarge, then EWD998Chan on the small node and the remaining seven models on od-4. A node's dive-bench was stopped once its last kept run was recorded; the run in progress at that moment was discarded, never recorded. Each row's runs_rep_node_wall_ms names the node of every repetition.

On od-1 the first D4 attempt was stopped after 47 minutes, during SlushLarge's first 1-worker run, by a defect in scripts/perf/release/node/d4-trim.sh (it treats a not-yet-created runs.jsonl as reaching its row limit). That run was discarded; SlushLarge's repetitions then ran in full as above.

dive-bench's golden check compares raw TLC counts and does not read conformance/expected-divergences.toml. At one worker the record names the registered entry for every run that differs from the golden exactly as registered (registered_divergence). Generated counts at more than one worker are diagnostics only (ADR 0086).
Release binary built on one bench node and copied to the others (independent builds were not byte-identical); dive_binary_sha256 names the copied binary.

nodes.od-1..od-4: the four on-demand D1 large-shard nodes, each on its own shard's models after its D1 pass
nodes.small: the D1 small-class node, after its D2, D3, D5 and D6 runs; same type, AMI, bootstrap and copied binaries

selection: The 48-model large class of the D1 record, less specifications/CheckpointCoordination/MCCheckpointCoordinationFailure.cfg: dive-bench needs a success golden, and that model's golden is a violation.

SlushLarge_with_D1_one_worker_time.note: D4's 1-worker SlushLarge runs stop at dive-bench's 3570 s time limit; D1 timed the same binary on the same host type at 5833.14 s to completion. Speed-ups against that time:

previous_record.reading: The medians fell because one-worker times fell more than multi-worker ones: temporal models whose 1-worker check got much faster (ElevatorLivenessLarge 449.8 s -> 2.1 s, aba_asyn_byz, cf1s_folklore) now sit near 1x, and MCKVsnap and SpanTreeRandom, refused at 4 and 8 workers before, now run sequentially at 1.00x. Per model, 4- and 8-worker wall times are lower than the previous record except where listed.
